identity.title: Egophony (E-to-A change) or bronchial breath sounds over a focal area

technique.how: Auscultate the posterior and lateral chest while the patient repeatedly says a sustained 'ee'; egophony is present where the sound is heard as a nasal 'ay' (A) over a focal area but as 'ee' elsewhere. Compare with breath sounds at the same site for a harsh, tubular bronchial quality with a pause between inspiration and expiration.
technique.prerequisites: Cooperative patient able to phonate; compare with the contralateral side at the same level.

interpretation.positive_finding: Focal E-to-A change and/or bronchial breath sounds over lung parenchyma, indicating consolidation or the compressed lung above an effusion.
interpretation.negative_finding: Normal vesicular sounds and 'ee' transmitted unchanged; absence has little rule-out value because the sign is insensitive.
interpretation.pitfalls: Sensitivity is low so most pneumonias lack egophony; it also occurs over the compressed lung at the upper border of a pleural effusion and can be mimicked at the trachea and interscapular area in thin patients.
interpretation.changes_what: Focal egophony in a febrile, coughing patient raises pneumonia probability substantially (LR+ about 6); proceed to CXR/LUS and empiric treatment as clinically indicated.

estimates.population: Adults with clinically suspected pneumonia or acute cough; 17 prospective cohorts (9 primary care, 7 ED); CAP prevalence 10% primary care, 20% ED

sources.citation: Ebell MH, Chupp H, Cai X, Bentivegna M, Kearney M. Accuracy of signs and symptoms for the diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia: a meta-analysis. Acad Emerg Med. 2020;27(7):541-553.
Metlay JP, Kapoor WN, Fine MJ. Does this patient have community-acquired pneumonia? Diagnosing pneumonia by history and physical examination. JAMA. 1997;278(17):1440-1445.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of egophony to withhold imaging in a patient with hypoxia, abnormal vital signs or immunocompromise.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Egophony plus hypotension, RR >30 or confusion suggests severe pneumonia; assess for sepsis and consider admission.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No pooled reliability statistic located in the sources viewed; the JAMA RCE (Metlay 1997) notes modest agreement for individual auscultatory signs but its table could not be viewed.

extraction_notes: Only the positive LR (6.17, 95% CI 1.34-18.0) was visible in the Ebell 2020 abstract; sensitivity, specificity and LR- for egophony are in the full text (not open access) and are therefore null. The Metlay 1997 JAMA RCE (PMID 9356004) is cited for context; its abstract contains no numbers and full text is not open access. Bronchial breath sounds were not separately quantified in any accessible source. Status set to partially_quantified because only one direction is reported.
